Source issues worth a reviewer's attention:
1. Reinhard eq. 1 as printed in the Utah tech report (page 4 image) is (1/N) exp(sum log(delta+L_w)), with 1/N outside the exponential. That is not a geometric mean. The intended log-average is exp((1/N) sum log(...)). I recorded the printed form with ocr=poor and flagged it in the entry. Check it against the SIGGRAPH 2002 version before the reboot implements it.
2. Reinhard's L_white is used as L/L_white^2 on the scaled luminance L, while the text defines L_white as L_max, a world-luminance quantity. The source is loose here. The notation entry flags it.
3. Stokes eq. 1.7a/1.7b as printed have typos. The 1.7a condition is written on unprimed (linear) symbols, and the G and B rows of 1.7b use R'. I recorded the corrected per-channel reading and flagged it in the notes.
4. Stokes Table 0.1 gives D65 y = 0.3291 and Table 0.2 gives y = 0.3290. The datum entry records the Table 0.2 value (0.3290) and notes the discrepancy.
5. The v1 code (archive/v1/src/colorimetry/cie_srgb.jl) uses IEC values (3.2406255..., threshold 0.0031308). The only local source is Stokes 1996, with 4-decimal matrices and thresholds 0.00304 and 0.03928. v1's values have no local source and should not be blessed from here.
6. The Stokes equations are GIF images, absent from refs/stokes_1996_srgb.txt. I read the GIFs (srgb09-13, 18, 19, 21, 22) directly. The result agrees with the orchestrator-added refs/stokes_1996_srgb_equations.txt. Anchors are nearby prose and ocr=poor throughout. image_verified is left unset for a reviewer. I also read Reinhard page 4 as an image, and those equation entries are ocr=poor because the fractions are split across lines in the text extraction.

The one I did NOT confirm on an image is PPP15 eq. 37 (p. 38, Gudmundsson fit exponents); it is read from the text layer only and flagged in its notes.

Findings from the sources that contradict v1 and CLAUDE.md:
- GH83 eq. 1 is the polar-cap radius R_cap = R^(3/2)(2π/cp)^(1/2), not the dipole |B|, so the v1 docstring citing 'GH Eq. 1' for |B| is wrong.
- The relation GH83 actually state is T^4 = T_pole^4 (sin^2 Φ + (K_perp/K_par) cos^2 Φ) with tan Φ = 2 cot β (eqs. 14-15), where Φ is the field inclination to the horizontal.
- PPP15 B.6 is the published modern colatitude profile, replacing the cos^2 ansatz. It equals 1 at θ=0 and 0 at θ=π/2 by inspection, giving a usable analytic check.

Other things for reviewers to check:
- g_14 is never explicitly defined in the PPP15 text; I took it as g in units of 1e14 cm s^-2 from figure captions, and flagged this in the entry.
- The gh83-approx-blackbody-emission note says eq. 18 has no redshift or light-bending factors. That is read from the printed formula, not stated in words.
- Cross-source notation entries cite a single source/anchor; the per-symbol source tags are in the meaning strings.
- PPP15 B.5 is explicitly rough (35% oscillations at B >> 1e13 G), recorded in the entry statement and in the fit-validity approximation.

harvest:rt.notes:
I read the page images and checked the text layer for the garbled equations (McPHAC pp. 3-4, 15-16; SPW09 pp. 3-5; VAL06 pp. 4 and 7). All 39 entries are status proposed. Provenance is set on the 35 non-notation entries, and check.py reports no errors or warnings for rt. The three provenance classes are 'derivable' for most equations, 'convention' for the emergent-intensity and Eddington-factor definitions, and 'fit' for the Eddington starting profile (with a reimplement route). Whole-DB check.py currently shows errors from other lanes' files, mostly symbol clashes (u, r, R, M, Z and others) and one short anchor in opacity.coulomb-log-classical. I did not touch those files. I renamed my own clashing symbols: y_col, z_vert, α_Bk, P_gas, g_surf, T_eff,atm, θ_Bn, and the (VAL06) suffixes on E_V, f_B and Y_e. Dedup should merge those with the other lanes' equivalents.

Flags a reviewer should check:
- rt.feautrier-discrete-mcphac: eq. 7 as printed has 2*rho_nu*dsigma/dmu with no 1/sigma_T,r factor. Eq. A1 does have 2*rho_nu/sigma_T,r, and eq. 4 has the equivalent 2/(kappa+sigma). So eq. 7 looks dimensionally inconsistent in the source itself. I reproduced the printed form and flagged it.
- rt.source-function-val: eq. 30 as printed mixes mode indices and an unprimed mu in the bracket [I^j(mu)+I^i(-mu)]. I left it as printed and marked ocr poor.
- rt.te-rybicki-matrices-mcphac: A14 defines a symbol printed as pi as Delta_1+Delta_2, and A19-A21 use it as pi*Delta. The weights b_k are never defined in the text. ocr is poor and image_verified is unset.
- rt.temperature-correction-spw09: the albedo alpha_nu^i is printed with a stray mu subscript on the second sigma-bar. The v1 code did not implement this scheme; it used an ad-hoc grey-body scaling at magnetic_atmosphere.jl:160.
- rt.no-feautrier-with-conversion-val: v1's P_jump post-processing swap is not the VAL06 scheme. VAL06 integrates with Runge-Kutta and applies the conversion at the resonance, because Feautrier cannot carry it.
- rt.vacuum-relevance-val: for B below about B_l (about 6.6e13 G at T=1e6 K, E=1 keV) the resonance lies outside both photospheres. This is likely the relevant regime for RX J1856, so P_jump conversion probably does not matter for that target.
- The VAL06 equations 1-3 were read from the page image. The text layer lost the exponent placement in eq. 3, and the unit of E_ad is not printed.
- I wrote the dipole-kernel normalisation check (integral over mu-prime equals sigma_T,r/2) as arithmetic on the printed formula. It is not a claim from the paper, and the notes say so.

Numerical cross-check (mpmath, in the scratchpad, not stored as entries): eq. 2.13 at R/2M = 1.6 gives (Delta phi)_max = 227.18 deg (source: 227). At R/2M = 1.76 it gives 180.05 deg, with b_max/R = 1.5218 (source: 1.52). The Delta phi(b) = pi root at R/2M = 1.6 gives b/R = 1.6206 (source: 1.621). b_max/R = 1.6330 (source: 1.633). Symbolic substitution rg = 2M, u = M/r shows Beloborodov eq. 9 and eq. 10 equal Pechenick 2.12 and 3.11 and the (u^r)^2 form of eq. 2.2; this is noted in the entries.

Issues for the orchestrator and reviewers:
1. Cross-domain symbol collisions. Other domain files have no conflicts_with entries, and I may not edit them. I therefore qualified my own sym strings where the bare symbol collides: 'b (impact)', 'mu (cos psi)', 'u (r_g/R)', 'u (M/r)', 'xi (sky)', 'M (G=c=1)', 'nu (observer)', 'nu (I_nu)'. For r, R, M, M_r and r_g (same concept as eos.notation-structure) I copied the eos meaning strings verbatim. If eos.notation-structure is reworded, my notation entries must be reworded to match. I dropped T_eff and L_ph from gr.notation-potekhin because surface.* already owns them.
2. Notation conflicts inside gr: alpha (Pechenick cap radius vs Beloborodov emission angle), lambda, phi. These are declared with conflicts_with on all four gr notation entries. gr.notation-geometry and gr.notation-radiation are adopted=true (Beloborodov/Potekhin CGS convention). Pechenick uses geometric units: M means GM/c^2, u = M/r = r_g/(2r), and the emission angle is delta.
3. Source inconsistency in Beloborodov, recorded in gr.beloborodov-cosine-error-bound: the abstract says 1% error for R = 3 r_g (pulsar formalism), the body says max 3% in the bending angle at alpha = 90 deg. The source does not reconcile them. Only the 3% figure is entered, as a datum.
4. The v1 docstring at archive/v1/src/geodesics/schwarzschild.jl:98 says u = 2/3 for R = 3 r_g. The correct value is u = r_g/R = 1/3. The v1 formula is correct; this is noted in gr.visible-fraction-cosine.
5. Inferences flagged in notes, not asserted as source text: in Beloborodov, I is frequency-integrated (from the I/nu^4 scaling), nu is the observer frequency and nu_0 the emitter frequency; the paper states neither. Beloborodov's u_t = 1, u_psi = b index positions were read from the image, and the metric signature is not stated.
6. Entries most worth a hostile review: gr.null-geodesic-constants (index positions); gr.observed-flux-element (eq. 11 factor bookkeeping); gr.metric-static-spherical (scope of the Phi boundary condition); gr.beloborodov-cosine-error-bound (which error measure); the three Pechenick numeric data (gr.dphi-max-r16, gr.circle180-radius-r16, gr.full-visibility-radius).

Schema change mid-run: SCHEMA.md and check.py gained a required `provenance` class. I added it to all 34 non-notation entries. 30 are derivable. Four are fit, each with a `reimplement` route: approx-ff-non-born-correction, vacuum-coeffs-fit, vacuum-resonance-energy, vacuum-resonance-density.

Symbol conflicts with other domains: I renamed my symbols to avoid them (b to b_rel, Z to Z_ion, A to A_ion, u to u_kT, nu to nu_loc, rho to rho_gas, xi to xi_vac, and eps/g/eta to eps_perp/g_gyro/eta_par). For B_12, a_m, E_V, f_B and Y_e I copied the existing eos/rt meaning strings exactly so they dedupe. The other symbols were not checked against the other domains.

Notable findings for reviewers:
1. The ref potekhin_chabrier_2003_ff_opacity is ApJ 585, 955, not A&A 399. CLAUDE.md's 'Appendix A' citation is wrong. The free-free formulae are in Sect. 4.3 (eqs. 37-54).
2. PC03's non-Born correction needs the Hummer (1988) Gaunt factor. The paper gives only the citation, not the fit, so the correction cannot be reproduced from refs/ alone. The approximation entry says so.
3. Neither PC03 nor PLCH04 gives the frame rotation that turns the PLCH04 eq. 18 mode vector (z along k, B in the x-z plane) into the cyclic components e_{j,alpha} (z along B) used by the opacity sums. The rotation is noted as something to derive and check.
4. v1 used the van Adelsberg and Lai K_+/- parametrisation, not PLCH04 eqs. 19-21. v1 also implemented the pp channel (PC03 eqs. 47-48), which PC03 calls negligible.
5. I read PDF page images for the equations of PC03 pp. 955, 958-959, 961, 963-964, PLCH04 pp. 2, 5-6, 9-10, McPHAC pp. 4-5 and PHC16 p. 6. Entries whose extracted text was garbled are ocr="poor" with latex taken from the image. Reviewers should confirm the grouping in PLCH04 eq. 21 (the trailing factor eps'/eta' sin^2/cos multiplies the whole fraction) and the PC03 eq. 44 and PHC16 eq. 2.13 layouts. image_verified is left unset.
6. I checked by hand that PC03 eqs. 37+41 at alpha=0, B->0 with Lambda=(pi/sqrt 3)g-bar reduce to McPHAC eq. 12. The check is noted in two entries.
7. The f_B function in vacuum-resonance-energy is defined by Ho and Lai 2003 eq. 2.41, which is not in refs/, so f_B cannot be computed from the local library.
